newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to set 15 pct fee on wheat exports.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to set 15 pct fee on wheat exports.

text.p: Bulgaria's trade ministry said on Friday it would propose to the cabinet next week to allow wheat exports under compulsory state registration regulations for traders and a 15 percent export fee, state BTA agency said.
"The export fee is to be calculated as 15 percent of the average spot price on major international commodity exchanges, effective from July 1," BTA said.
Wheat exports have been banned in Bulgaria since October 1995 after excessive shipments caused a severe grain shortage.
The ministry would also propose an export fee of $25-30 per tonne on wheat bran, wheat flour and feed wheat.
Under agriculture ministry projections, Bulgaria expects 2.4 million tonnes of wheat from this year's crop.
Bulgaria pledged to liberalise foreign trade regulations under a $657 million reform and funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund.
